text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Head of state General Sani Abacha tells convention of quantity surveyors that henceforth Nigerian professionals will be favoured in executing government contracts.
- In a message to passing out parade of youth service scheme by newly qualified graduates, Abacha says there will be no stopping the war against corruption in the country.
- Nigerian petrochemical plant may shut over its inability to pay for raw materials, a senior oil official says.
- Central bank declares budget deficit of 6.58 billion naira for first half of 1996 in contrast to eight billion naira surplus given by Finance Minister Anthony Ani last month.
- University teachers formally suspend seven-month-old strike which was broken long ago.
- Central bank reports small growth in Nigeria's industrial sector for first half of 1996, says capacity utilisation rose to 32.5 percent from 29.4 percent in the second half of last year.
- Central bank says Nigeria's external debt down slightly to $31.99 billion in first half of 1996 from $32.581 billion at the end of last year.
